course_name_original: Fundamentals of Electric Power Systems Engineering
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Electric Power Systems Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Student knows the principles of electricity generation.
Student knows the operating principles of electric power systems and the processes of transmission, distribution, and delivery of electricity to the consumer.
Student can perform basic calculations related to electric power networks.
Student can analyze basic phenomena in electric power systems.
Student is able to think and act consciously regarding the energy needs of the modern world.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to exercises. Two-ports and operations on two-ports.
Equivalent circuits of system components.
Current and power flow in open and double-sided fed networks.
Calculation of voltage drops in open and double-sided fed networks.
Selected methods of voltage regulation in a distribution network.
Active power and energy losses in electric power system components.
Economics of transformer operation.
Reactive power compensation.
Fundamentals of short-circuit calculations. Calculation of short-circuit power and currents.
Selection of conductor cross-section according to selected criteria.
Reliability calculation of simple network systems.
Electric power systems.
Electricity generation in professional power plants.
Operation of power plants in the electric power system.
Unconventional energy sources. Renewable energy.
Power transformers.
Power lines.
Basic calculations of electric power systems.
Electric power network configurations.
Electric power substations.
Reliability of electric power systems.
Disturbances in the operation of electric power systems.
Quality of electrical energy.
Ecological aspects in electric power engineering.
SmartGrid - 'intelligent' electric power systems.
teaching_methods: Distance learning methods and techniques (E-learning, remote learning)
assessment_rules: Attendance at lectures is considered a form of activity. For auditorium classes, positive completion of colloquia is required. The final grade for auditorium classes can be based on oral or written statements in the form of a colloquium, which, according to AGH study regulations, translates into the final grade for this form of classes.
